headline: South Asia: ‘Why the need for all this drama’: DG ISPR lampoons India's 'neutralised Pakistani terrorist' claims, presents him before media
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: ‘Why the need for all this drama’: DG ISPR lampoons India's 'neutralised Pakistani terrorist' claims, presents him before media.
- India: US Imposes Sanctions On Iran's Rail, Auto Sectors To Raise Economic Pressure.
- Western Russia: Ukraine has limited contingency plans for Russian attacks on water supply – NYT.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Navy awards RTX’s Raytheon $24.4B for SM-6 missiles amid stockpile concerns.
- Military Times, 13 hours ago: US Navy awards RTX’s Raytheon $24.4B for SM-6 missiles amid stockpile concerns.
The deal for the SM-6 interceptors comes as the Pentagon pushes to replenish munitions stockpiles depleted by conflicts in the Middle East.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: Navy Expeditionary Combat Command rebranded to reflect warfare evolution.
CNO Adm. Daryl Caudle announced that the Navy Expeditionary Combat Command will now be known as Commander, Navy Expeditionary Forces.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: Boeing adds to big week with first full-rate Grey Wolf helicopter order.
The U.S. Air Force awarded Boeing a roughly $85 million contract for four more MH-139A Grey Wolf helicopters, with the first under full-rate production.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Doctors demand timeline for IDT ruling.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Doctors demand timeline for IDT ruling.
The Jamaica Medical Doctors Association (JMDA) is calling for the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to provide a timeline for delivering its ruling in the longstanding dispute between doctors and the Ministry of Health and Wellness over overtime payments. In a press release, JMDA President Jubilee Brown-Service said it took note of the IDT’s September 30 statement, which conceded that “justice delayed is justice denied”. “We call on the IDT to stop denying justice to our doctors by handing down its award without further delay,” the JMDA declared.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 17 hours ago: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.
Federico Aramburú, who was killed in March 2022 after a bar brawl, will lend his name to a social commitment award La entrada Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Ukraine has limited contingency plans for Russian attacks on water supply – NYT.
- Ukrainska Pravda, The Moscow Times, one hour ago: Ukraine has limited contingency plans for Russian attacks on water supply – NYT.
Ukrainian officials are concerned that the country has limited contingency plans for major water supply disruptions if Russia launches large-scale strikes on water infrastructure.
- The Moscow Times, 19 hours ago: Putin Says World Is Living Through a Dangerous Moment, Warns West Not to Escalate.
He reiterated that Moscow would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad was threatened.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russian attack damages Kherson local history museum and World War II-era howitzer.
A Russian attack on Kherson has damaged the regional local history museum, a protected early 20th-century monument, and a World War II-era M-30 howitzer.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: NYT reveals Russian plan to attack Ukraine's energy system.
The New York Times reports that Russia plans a three-stage attack on Ukraine's energy system, targeting substations, hydro plants and nuclear facilities.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Thousands in Kosovo Protest Again for ‘Fair Justice’ After Hague Convictions.
- Balkan Insight, 19 hours ago: Thousands in Kosovo Protest Again for ‘Fair Justice’ After Hague Convictions.
Large crowds attend rally in Pristina against Hague court verdict convicting four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders of war crimes, with protest speaker attacking 'double standards when it comes to justice'.
- Politico Europe, 9 hours ago: Russia’s not-quite-war on Europe.
Europe’s gray-zone war with Russia is getting harder to ignore. Sarah Wheaton speaks to security expert and author Elisabeth Braw about how Europe should respond as sabotage, arson, cyberattacks and attacks on critical infrastructure become more frequent and more dangerous, who pays when businesses are targeted, and what happens when one of them turns deadly. […]
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: How a failed attack in Leipzig revealed a wider Russian campaign.
Documents obtained by the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network trace drone bombs, incendiary parcels and arson attacks to Russian intelligence.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: Tories warn Burnham’s EU ‘pandering’ will shred post-Brexit trade deals.
Three former ministers tell POLITICO of “grave consequences” if the U.K. moves closer to the EU under prime minister's bid for a revamped relationship.

AFRICA

- Africanews, 22 hours ago: Mass funeral held in Gaza City after 105 bodies recovered from rubble.
Hundreds of mourners in Gaza City held a vigil on Wednesday for 105 people killed during Israel's war on the Palestinian territory. Their bodies were recovered in the past several days, after remaining buried under the rubble for nearly three years.

[Vanguard] Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised 16 terrorists and recovered weapons after repelling simultaneous attacks in Adamawa.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 2 hours ago: Uganda: Uganda to Host Inaugural Conference On Military Operations Other Than War.
[Nile Post] Uganda will next week host the inaugural Conference on Military Operations Other Than War (MOOTW), bringing together military commanders, regional security bodies and peace support mission leaders from across Africa to discuss emerging security threats and non-traditional approaches to conflict management.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 6 hours ago: Sudan: Women's Groups Report Widespread Sexual Violence and Detention Across Sudan.
[Dabanga] Women's rights groups have reported widespread sexual violence, exploitation and detention of women and girls across Sudan, warning that fear, insecurity and restrictions on documentation are masking the scale of abuses.

According to the wounded pilot, Capt. Smit Machchhar, he had opened the cockpit door while on the floor of the plane and actively being attacked by his Omani copilot.

The journalists' identities and terrorist affiliations were verified using documents released by the terrorist organizations themselves and materials recovered by IDF troops during Gaza operations.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Iran weighing options against US, Israel as nuclear talks stall, Israeli defense official says.
A senior Israeli defense official said Iran's room for maneuver has narrowed amid US sanctions, while Israel is preparing for the possibility that an Iranian move could spiral out of control.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Stanbic Bank Zim to Finance Chirundu Border Post Upgrade Project.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 3 hours ago: South Africa: Would Homegrown LEN Cost More? Why SA Should Still Make the HIV Prevention Jab.
[Bhekisisa] South Africa wants to make the six-monthly HIV prevention injection lenacapavir locally. But cheaper generics made elsewhere are expected from 2027. Vinodh Aroon Edward explains why getting the jab to people quickly must come first -- while South Africa builds the skills to make it here.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Chivayo, Wife, Three Others' Heavily Dismembered Bodies Removed From Crash Site After 18-Hour Operation.
[New Zimbabwe] THE heavily dismembered bodies of controversial businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife Lucy Muteke and three others killed in a plane crash were finally removed from the wreckage site about 18 hours after the tragedy.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: Zimbabwe: NPA Goes Pink in Push for Early Breast Cancer Detection.
[263Chat] The National Prosecuting Authority of Zimbabwe (NPAZ) has joined the global campaign to raise awareness about breast cancer, calling on women and communities to prioritise breast health and early detection.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: ‘Why the need for all this drama’: DG ISPR lampoons India's 'neutralised Pakistani terrorist' claims, presents him before media.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 18 hours ago: ‘Why the need for all this drama’: DG ISPR lampoons India's 'neutralised Pakistani terrorist' claims, presents him before media.
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference on Thursday. The press briefing came after Indian media reported that an individual wanted in connection with the April 22 Pahalgam terrorist attack last year had been killed during an “encounter” in Indian Illegally Occupied Kashmir’s Korag area.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina.
Pakistan on Friday strongly condemned an attack by the Houthi militia on the Taibah power distribution station in Madina on Sept 29, describing it as a “grave provocation” and a threat to regional peace and security. In a statement, the Foreign Office (FO) said the attack targeted civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Holy Prophet’s (PBUH) Mosque. “The sanctity of the Two Holy Mosques and the safety of worshippers and pilgrims must be respected under all circumstances,” the FO said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Trump calls Iran’s Hormuz offer ‘not enough’.
• US president warns strikes against Tehran could resume after midterms; Washington sanctions Iran’s top carmakers, rail operators • Pezeshkian says his country is open to dialogue; Putin hopes the strait reopens, says Russia’s offer to take enriched uranium still stands PRESIDENT Donald Trump rejected Iran’s offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as “simply not enough”, warning that military action against Tehran could resume after the midterm elections and predicting long-term peace with the country is unlikely.
- The Hindu - International, 19 hours ago: Pakistan says killed 22 terrorists in airstrikes in Afghanistan.
Afghanistan's Taliban government, meanwhile, said that Pakistani strikes killed nine Afghan civilians, including women and children, and injured 11 others.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt and its strike group carrying the service members would arrive in the Middle East by the end of November. Currently two other aircraft carriers are stationed in the region -- the USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Jamie Dimon warns Europe again: 'You may be losing,' offers a solution.
Jamie Dimon has advocated for a groundbreaking free-trade agreement between the United States and Europe to boost economic progress. He insists Europe must implement essential economic and military reforms to enhance competitiveness. Dimon envisions that a united front among democratic nations can effectively tackle geopolitical challenges and establish global trade benchmarks while simultaneously strengthening the American economy and democratic partnerships.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Will Russian oil be economically viable for India if Trump tariffs return?.
Russia became an unusually attractive supplier when Western buyers retreated after the war with Ukraine. Its share of Indian crude imports, below 2% before the war, expanded rapidly as discounts compensated refiners for longer supply chains. In the present day, the situation has become more complex, the new US law potentially changes the economics of India’s Russian oil purchases.

- South China Morning Post - China, Africanews, 3 hours ago: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties as northern fighting escalates.
Ethiopia and Eritrea broke diplomatic ties on Thursday, accusing each other of stoking internal conflicts as fighting continued in northern Ethiopia. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing a rebel group, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which launched a major assault against government forces last week, raising fears of a return to the devastating 2020–2022 civil war that killed an estimated 600,000 people.
